mission: At the relay mast, Sera reads Veraine through her construction choices and Desh claims the sabotage role before anyone has to ask him.
why_now: The plan cannot stay theoretical. The group needs to touch the enemy's work, see what it implies, and assign the human cost of acting against it.
conflict: Sera is reading a mind through metal. Desh is recognizing that the plan fails unless he takes the most exposed task himself.
turning_point: Sera identifies the mast as Veraine's work, and Desh volunteers in the same breath of understanding.
opening_hook: The three of them walk the kilometre to the ridge-mast in silence that is not uncomfortable. Ben has the Codex notes folded in a pocket that does not matter. Sera's stride matches Desh's on ground neither of them grew up on
closing_hook: Two plans, both dependent on trust: the resonance trio needs Kael; the sabotage needs Desh alone against armed opposition. Both plans fail without both parts. Sera's hand on the mast base still echoing in Ben's chest
emotional_trajectory: Tactical approach to the mast -> Sera's silent read -> her four-word verdict -> Desh's willing commitment -> the interlocking dependency

stakes.personal: Desh's arc lands — the choice unmistakable; Sera's expertise directly shaping the group's understanding of their opponent for the second book-level time (first: Ch 21 s1)
stakes.interpersonal: The group becoming a genuine team through voluntary specialisation; Sera's expert read landing as a statement the others receive without answering
stakes.external: The two-pronged plan is the only path to defeating Veraine and saving the seal; Veraine's design-authorship of the array is now a felt fact, not a deduced one

setting: Veranthos — ridge a kilometre from camp, nearest amplification array component (a relay mast)
sensory_details: The mast itself — taller than expected, components that do not quite match any manufacturer's standard loadout, the specific curvature of the load-distribution antennas hand-shaped rather than stamped; Ash-Tithe assembly marks at the base: ash-white tally lines, Pira Kul's pressure-cut neatness, Vess Oran's salvage labels half-scraped away; the base-plate's harmonic geometry subtle enough that only a trained eye finds it; Sera's hand flat against the base-plate, palm warming on the metal, the specific micro-shift of her face when a design-signature resolves and separates Veraine's mind from her crew's work; the small Dantari exhalation she releases when she finishes reading; Desh at the edge of the clearing with his datapad open, approach-telemetry overlaid on the array schematic, three component-locations lighting up as his fingers trace them; the ridge wind; the valley beyond with the Scar visible as a line of heat shimmer without heat; Ben's own hand on the Codex-notes pocket without taking them out
canon_elements_needed: Sith design-signature theory for Force-amplification architecture
Brotherhood-of-Darkness inheritance conventions (for what Veraine's signature is deviating from)
action_beats: The three walk the kilometre to the relay mast on the ridge in uncomfortable but not uncomforted silence
Sera circles the mast once, separating crew assembly marks from Veraine's design logic, then lays her hand flat on the base-plate and closes her eyes briefly; Ben watches her face change
Sera says, without opening her eyes: 'This is her mind.' She does not elaborate
Desh, at the clearing's edge, finishes tracing the three critical component-locations on his datapad; his expression goes clinical
Desh volunteers before anyone asks — straightening from the datapad with his decision already made: 'That's my job. Let the Force-users do the Force thing. I'll handle the part that requires hands.'
The three walk back toward camp. None of them comments on Sera's four words. All three of them are carrying the weight
notes: Keep the scene tactile and spare. Sera's line should land once, and Desh's volunteer should feel matter-of-fact because he has already decided.

turning_point_detail.trigger: Sera identifies the mast as Veraine's work through her hand-reading of the base-plate geometry, and in the same breath of understanding, Desh volunteers for the sabotage role.
turning_point_detail.shift: The scene dynamics pivot from tactical reconnaissance to emotional commitment. Ben moves from observing Sera's expertise to witnessing Desh's willing acceptance of the most dangerous task. The pressure that was abstract becomes embodied.
turning_point_detail.cost: Ben carries the weight of the interlocking dependency: both plans fail without both parts. Desh's choice is unmistakable and voluntary, which means Ben cannot protect him from it. Sera's silent read—'This is her mind'—becomes a statement the group receives without answering, deepening the isolation of each person's role.

emotional_arc.start: Tactical approach—Ben is focused on the mission, moving through the landscape with purpose and minimal internal noise.
emotional_arc.shift: Sera's silent read and four-word verdict shift Ben's emotional register from tactical to witnessing. The pressure tightens around what Sera has just revealed and what Desh is about to choose.
emotional_arc.end: Interlocking dependency—Ben understands that both plans fail without both parts, and that Desh has already decided. The weight is no longer abstract; it is carried by three people walking back in silence.

key_beats.beat_description: The three walk the kilometre to the relay mast on the ridge in silence that is not uncomfortable—Ben carrying the Codex notes in a pocket that does not matter, Sera's stride matching Desh's on ground neither of them grew up on.
key_beats.state_change: The opening pressure becomes concrete instead of abstract. The group is moving toward the evidence.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's instinct pushes toward action rather than explanation. The silence is not empty; it is the silence of people who have already decided to move. His hand-awareness of the Codex notes in his pocket registers as a small, unnecessary weight—the intellectual work is done; now comes the physical work.

key_beats.beat_description: Sera circles the mast once, lays her hand flat on the base-plate, and closes her eyes briefly. Ben watches her face change—the micro-shift that signals recognition resolving into certainty.
key_beats.state_change: Pressure escalates. Sera's material-reading is active; the mast is no longer a theoretical component but a text she is reading.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben's focus tightens on what is changing in Sera's face. The moment stretches slightly—not melodramatic, but present. He recognizes the signature of her expertise landing, the small exhalation that follows when a design-signature resolves. His own breath steadies in response, matching the rhythm of her certainty.

key_beats.beat_description: Sera says, without opening her eyes: 'This is her mind.' She does not elaborate. The statement lands once and holds.
key_beats.state_change: Sera's expert read becomes a felt fact, not a deduced one. Veraine's authorship of the array is now present in the room—or on the ridge, in the metal.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben receives the statement without answering. The four words are complete; they do not require response. His chest tightens slightly—not fear, but the pressure of understanding that Sera has just named something that cannot be un-named. The isolation of her expertise becomes visible: she has read something the others cannot read, and she has delivered it without softening or explanation.

key_beats.beat_description: Desh, at the clearing's edge, finishes tracing the three critical component-locations on his datapad. His expression goes clinical—the shift from observer to actor. He straightens from the datapad with his decision already made.
key_beats.state_change: The scene pivots. Desh is no longer waiting for assignment; he is claiming the role. The pressure that was on Sera now moves toward Desh's choice.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben recognizes the moment Desh's decision crystallizes. It is not a moment of doubt or hesitation; it is the moment when someone stops thinking and starts acting. Ben's own body registers this—a small shift in posture, a readiness for what comes next. The clinical expression on Desh's face is not coldness; it is focus. Ben understands that Desh has already calculated the cost and chosen to pay it.

key_beats.beat_description: Desh volunteers before anyone asks—straightening from the datapad with his decision already made: 'That's my job. Let the Force-users do the Force thing. I'll handle the part that requires hands.' The statement is matter-of-fact, not heroic.
key_beats.state_change: The two-pronged plan is now dependent on both parts. Both plans fail without both roles filled. The human cost of acting against Veraine is now assigned and accepted.
key_beats.pov_reaction: Ben carries the weight of the interlocking dependency. Desh's choice is unmistakable and voluntary, which means Ben cannot protect him from it. The pressure that was abstract becomes embodied in three people walking back toward camp. Ben's hand-awareness of Sera's touch on the mast base—the specific warmth of her palm on the metal—echoes in his chest as they move. The silence on the return walk is not uncomfortable; it is the silence of people who have just made a choice that cannot be unmade.

anti_patterns: Keep the scene tactile and spare—do not elaborate.
Sera's line should land once without elaboration.
Desh's volunteer should feel matter-of-fact because he has already decided—do not soften with doubt.
Do not arrive at clinical articulation of Veraine's design signature.
Do not describe the Force-wound in diagnostic voice.
